parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Chilliwack · The Landing
MLS® uses Lower Landing as a sub-area name within the City of Chilliwack, and the City has not published a boundary for it.
The closest official description is the City’s Greenspace Plan 2020, which lists The Landing among its community parks.

The area takes its name from the Landing recreation lands on the north side of Chilliwack, by the Fraser River: the Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre at Unit #1, 9145 Corbould Street and the Landing Sports Centre at 45530 Spadina Avenue.
MLS® listings also group the Cedarbrook development on Schweyey Road into this sub-area. That is an MLS grouping, not an official boundary.

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Lower Landing

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500 (Chilliwack 2050) was adopted on December 16, 2025.
ALR: Published municipal records list no ALR statement for this sub-area. ALR status is set address by address.
Flood: the Fraser River floodplain is designated under the City’s Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519. The minimum building setback is 60 m from the natural boundary of the Fraser River.
The City maintains an extensive diking network protecting the community from the Fraser and Vedder River systems.

A 2014 provincial study updated Fraser River flood water elevations using the 1894 flood of record. Many dike sections need raising, by up to 0.8 m in the worst locations, to meet the provincial standard of the flood profile plus 0.6 m of freeboard.

The East Dike near the CHIP intake protects the majority of the Chilliwack floodplain. The McGillivray Pump Station was upgraded in 2019, and Fraser River erosion protection work was done in 2019 and 2022.

A BC Government news release lists the Skwah First Nation Flood Protection Project, with the City of Chilliwack and Shxwhá:y Village as regional partners, at $5,890,000 in disaster-risk-reduction funding.

How do I get around from Lower Landing?

BC Transit’s Chilliwack routes are 51 Vedder, 52 Evans, 53 Fairfield, 54 Promontory, 55 Yarrow – Greendale, 57 Broadway, 58 Tyson, 59 Industrial, 66 Fraser Valley Express, 71 Agassiz-Harrison and 72 Hope.

Fraser Valley Express, route 66, is a regional service linking Chilliwack with Lougheed Town Centre Station, calling at McCallum Park and Ride, Highstreet Exchange and Carvolth Exchange along the way. In Chilliwack it stops at the Lickman Park and Ride, Downtown Chilliwack, and Vedder Rd at Luckakuck Way.
